### Industry Best Practice for Captive Gateway DNS
The next step is to detail the low-level design for each component, including network configuration and the captive portal implementation on the Gateway node.

The system comprises multiple ESP32 nodes forming a repeater network. A designated "Gateway" node connects to an external WAN (Wide Area Network) and acts as the internet gateway for the entire network. All other nodes (Repeater nodes) extend the network coverage by connecting to the Gateway or another Repeater node's AP and creating their own AP for downstream devices or repeaters.
Client devices connect to any node's AP interface and are redirected to a captive portal hosted on the Gateway node for internet access authentication.

## 2. Captive Portal Implementation (Gateway Node Only)
*   Implement a lightweight local DNS server by opening a UDP socket on port 53 on the Gateway node. This will be the sole DNS server for all clients connected to the AP.
*   The server will parse incoming DNS queries. For all A/AAAA record requests from unauthenticated clients, it will respond with the Gateway's AP IP address.
*   Host a simple web server exclusively on the Gateway node using `esp_http_server_start()`.
*   Most modern operating systems attempt to connect to known URLs to detect captive portals. The HTTP server on the Gateway must handle these requests correctly to trigger the captive portal popup.
*   When a client clicks the button on the Gateway, its IP address will be added to the authenticated list.
*   For unauthenticated clients, the DNS server will always respond with the Gateway's IP address, redirecting all traffic to the captive portal.
